title: WaterPilot Supported-Capability Matrix
description: Which data capabilities WaterPilot can technically support, their candidate source families, and whether they need local measurement or can be inferred from imagery. PROPOSED pending domain review. technicalSupport describes whether a method/source family exists in principle; it says NOTHING about whether any particular area has onboarded, validated data — that is area readiness, assessed per area by data-readiness-gate.md. Values not ready for an area render as 'unavailable', never 0.

technicalSupport.supported: A deterministic method and a candidate source family exist; once a validated, authorized source is onboarded for an area, the capability can be produced without a new model. Does not imply any area is ready.
technicalSupport.provisional: Partially derivable; needs caveats and/or a reviewed model even with validated data.
technicalSupport.unavailable: No adequate method without local measurement and/or a reviewed model that WaterPilot does not yet have.

capabilities.notes: Gridded precipitation is available from EE, but converting rainfall to usable supply (runoff/harvesting) needs a reviewed response model (see metrics.md). Rainfall depth itself is observable; supply impact is not a flat percentage.

Volume pumped from groundwater into supply (MLD), from metered pumping/borewell records. A supply contribution, not an aquifer-state measure: abstraction data says nothing about groundwater level or sustainability.

Aquifer water-table level and trend (m bgl) require in-situ monitoring-well measurements. Satellite proxies (e.g. GRACE) are coarse and not a substitute at community scale. Distinct from groundwater_abstraction volumes.
Surface-water extent/occurrence is observable from imagery; converting extent to usable volume/yield needs bathymetry/assumptions and review.
Drinking-water quality (chemical/biological) cannot be inferred from imagery. Requires sampled measurements. Unavailable until local data onboarded.
Terrain/DEM and past flood extents help, but calibrated flood risk needs hydrological/drainage modelling and review. Not inferable from a single imagery layer.

Land cover / built-up fraction is a standard imagery-derived product with documented classes; technically the most directly supportable, subject to licence authorization and class mapping. No source is onboarded for any area yet.
Piped/tanker supply volumes and reliability come from utility/operator records, not imagery. Required for demand/supply/deficit metrics. Unavailable until onboarded.

Neighbour/shared-aquifer hydraulic effects need a coupled groundwater model + boundary evidence. Distance alone never becomes a validated impact score. Unavailable until adequate coupled evidence exists.
